sample_unit: third-year medical students (research proposals with AI chat transcripts)

links.outcome: Medical students' verification and critical thinking of AI outputs, rubric score 0-3
links.effect: Verification & Critical Thinking M = 0.41 (SD = 0.71) out of 3, significantly lower than Transparency (2.08) and Integration (1.64); overall applied AI literacy score 5.47/12.
links.quote: Domain-level analysis revealed the highest performance in Transparency (M = 2.08, SD = 0.55) and Integration (M = 1.64, SD = 0.67), while Purposefulness (M = 1.33, SD = 0.69) and Verification & Critical Thinking (M = 0.41, SD = 0.71) were significantly lower.

links.outcome: Extent to which students verified AI-generated content and recognized bias
links.effect: Verification & Critical Thinking (bias recognition) scored M = 0.41 (SD = 0.71) of 3, the lowest of four domains (Friedman χ²(3) = 50.36, p < 0.001).
links.quote: Domain-level analysis revealed the highest performance in Transparency (M = 2.08, SD = 0.55) and Integration (M = 1.64, SD = 0.67), while Purposefulness (M = 1.33, SD = 0.69) and Verification & Critical Thinking (M = 0.41, SD = 0.71) were significantly lower.

unlisted_practices: Performance-based rubric assessment of applied AI literacy using authentic AI chat transcripts in medical education
Targeted instruction and authentic assessment on AI use in medical curricula

screen.reason: Evaluates medical students' applied AI literacy (prompting, verification, critical thinking) using chat transcripts from a coursework task, but does not test a specific deployment intervention or safeguard.
